reasoning_steps: Under the modern budget process established by the Congressional Budget Act of 1974, Congress is required to pass all regular appropriations bills before the new fiscal year begins on October 1
Since the law took effect in fiscal year 1977, Congress has passed all of its regular appropriations measures on time in only four fiscal years: 1977, 1989, 1995, and 1997

In every year since fiscal year 1997, Congress has failed to enact all required regular appropriations bills prior to the October 1 deadline, instead relying on continuing resolutions or late omnibus spending packages.
